form: This is the third in a trilogy of ICSNL articles on infinitives in St’át’imcets. Each deals with one of the three main classes of infinitives found in the language: Davis (2020) examines raising infinitives with c̓íla ‘seem, (be) like, resemble’, Davis (2025) investigates control infinitives with epistemic verbs such as zəwátən ‘know’ and x̌əkxít ‘instruct’, and here in the third I turn to infinitival complements to evaluative adjectives such as ̣x̌aƛ̓ ‘hard’, qʷámqʷmət ‘fun’, and k̓ínk̓ənt dangerous’.
